description: The Commander observed a marked improvement in crew morale and cohesion by Sol 6, in explicit contrast to the early-mission stress of Sols 1-4 (snowfall on arrival, the wall-heater install rush, and early operational pressure). The XO described the crew as now 'operating like a unit,' with the early stress having 'forged something solid.'
response: No formal intervention was needed; cohesion emerged through shared task completion (successful EVAs, sample collection) over the first six sols.
lesson: Expect and normalise an early-mission stress dip; do not over-react to Sol 1-4 friction. Track morale qualitatively sol-over-sol as an early-warning and reassurance signal, not only after problems arise.
source_citation: SRC-flashline-crew-reports, AMARUQ (CREW 18) SOL 6 REPORT (29-7-2025), lines 64-73. Sol: explicit from report header. Confidence (C) rationale: subjective narrative quotes attributed to crew roles, not a measured psychological instrument.
